title: Homework Works if Homework Quality Is High: Using Multilevel Modeling to Predict the Development of Achievement in Mathematics https://psycnet.apa.org/record/2010-08635-015
author: Barton, Craig
source: Tips for Teachers (tipsforteachers.co.uk), December 17, 2024 — original paper:
summary: This page summarises Dettmers and colleagues' multilevel study of homework quality (not just quantity) in a large longitudinal sample of German high school mathematics students, distinguishing between task selection (how well-chosen and integrated the homework is) and cognitive challenge (how demanding it is). Well-selected homework consistently predicted higher student motivation, effort, and achievement gains. Cognitively challenging homework showed a more complex picture: it benefited achievement at the class level but did not necessarily translate to individual-level benefit, and overly demanding tasks risked undermining students' confidence and effort. Barton draws out the practical balance the authors recommend: pitch tasks at a genuinely engaging, well-integrated level that stretches students without overwhelming them, and consider individualizing difficulty or offering tasks solvable via multiple methods of varying complexity so different students can access an appropriate level of challenge. The authors frame this as evidence that teacher training should focus more directly on the quality of homework design, not just how much homework to set.
points: Well-selected, well-integrated homework -- not just homework quantity -- predicts higher student motivation, effort, and achievement gains.
Cognitively demanding homework helps achievement at the class level but doesn't reliably help at the individual level, and can undermine confidence if overly demanding.
Teachers should aim to individualize homework challenge to match students' prior knowledge and cognitive ability where feasible.
Offering tasks solvable through multiple methods of varying complexity lets different students access an appropriate level of challenge within the same assignment.
quotes: Our study provides strong evidence that interesting and well-selected homework assignments are associated with higher expectancy and value beliefs and with higher homework effort and that they are effective for learning

Teachers should carefully select homework assignments that are interesting and well-integrated into the lessons to enhance student understanding. Students who perceived that their homework was well-selected reported higher levels of motivation and effort, and showed greater achievement gains
Teachers should aim for a balance between assigning adequately difficult tasks to improve motivation and effort, and challenging but well-structured tasks to foster performance
Teachers may consider offering individualized homework tasks that challenge but do not overwhelm individual students, taking into account their prior knowledge and cognitive abilities
Another approach is to assign tasks that can be solved using various methods with differing levels of complexity
